finding.claim: With caching enabled, a token that has a numeric exp but no numeric iat is cached for the full cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) and is not checked against exp on a cache hit. After the token expires, the verifier still returns the cached payload as valid. The same applies to nbf/maxAge, which are only recorded when iat is present.
finding.source: A signed token that has exp but no iat claim. Tokens from third-party issuers often omit iat. The verifier must have the cache option enabled. The attacker only needs to hold a legitimately issued token and replay it after it expires.
finding.sink: The cache-hit branch in verify() (src/verifier.js:363-378) returns the cached payload without re-validating exp.

trace.note: A token that passes verifyToken is passed to cacheSet(cacheContext, payload).
hasIat is false when payload.iat is not a number.
The block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp or maxAge) only runs when hasIat is true. Otherwise cacheValue stays [value, 0, 0].
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, and cacheValue[2] === 0 is replaced by maxTTL. The token's real exp is never used.
A later call with the same token reads [value, min, max] from the cache.
min === 0 and now <= max, so the cached payload is returned at line 377. verifyToken is skipped and the exp validator never runs.

finding.guards_checked: The exp validator at src/verifier.js:304-323 only runs on a cache miss. The cache-hit time-window check at 368-375 uses only the min and max stored by cacheSet. cacheTTL caps the window at 10 minutes by default but does not remove it. The decoder and signature checks are enforced correctly, so this is only a post-expiry acceptance window. Applications that always issue iat are not affected.
